newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: REESINK PROFITS DIVE 40 PCT. [CORRECTED 13:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: REESINK PROFITS DIVE 40 PCT. [CORRECTED 13:50 GMT]

text.p: Technical wholesaler Reesink said on Thursday its first quarter 1997 profits were down 40 percent on the previous year. It gave no precise figures.
(Corrects to show comparison is year on year.)
As a result of the poor profit trends Reesink would shortly mount a restructuring programme, it said.
It said the costs involved would be covered by existing provisions.
Reesink said that in its recently published 1996 annual report it had cautioned that it was well behind schedule in achieving the targets it had set itself for 1997.

"At the end of the first quarter this trend transpired to have continued...Profits transpired to have fallen by some 40 percent compared with the result of the first three months of last year," it said.
It said that these calculations were based on a cost burden in the form of provisions equal to those of 1996. "The level of actual provisions will be determined at the half-year result," it added.
Reesink said all the markets in which its subsidiaries were active had been disappointing and that its activities in the agricultural sector had performed particularly badly.
"The willingness to invest in this segment fell below any level hitherto envisaged," it said.
